standard_prerequisites.name: K-injective complexes and the fact that an acyclic K-injective complex is homotopy equivalent to zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the device that turns the vanishing of Ext groups into the vanishing of maps in the derived category.

standard_prerequisites.name: The adjunction identifying Hom over A from A_f with Hom over A_f after applying Hom_A(A_f, -)
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets a map out of an A_f-complex be rewritten as a map into Hom_A(A_f, I^bullet).

standard_prerequisites.name: The explicit two-term free resolution of A_f and the construction of derived limits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: written out at proof lines 25887-25895 and invoked at proof lines 25902-25905
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the displayed pro-product map in condition (7) and the identification of T(K, f) with R Hom_A(A_f, K).

standard_prerequisites.name: Ext spectral sequence of a two-term projective resolution and its degeneration
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the short exact sequences that relate Ext^p_A(A_f, K) to Hom and Ext^1 of the cohomology modules.

core_obligations: Observe the trivial implications (2) => (1) and the equivalence of (1) with (6) (proof line 25869).
Assume (1), choose a K-injective complex I^bullet representing K, and read (1) as the acyclicity of Hom_A(A_f, I^bullet) (proof lines 25870-25871).

Compute Hom_{D(A)}(E, K) for E represented by a complex M^bullet of A_f-modules, rewrite it as Hom_{K(A_f)}(M^bullet, Hom_A(A_f, I^bullet)) by the adjunction, and use that the latter is K-injective and acyclic so that it is homotopy equivalent to zero, deducing (2) (proof lines 25872-25884).

Write down the explicit free resolution 0 -> oplus_N A -> oplus_N A -> A_f -> 0 with the displayed maps and apply Hom_A(-, I^bullet) to obtain 0 -> Hom_A(A_f, I^bullet) -> prod I^bullet -> prod I^bullet -> 0, identifying prod I^bullet as a representative of prod_{n >= 0} K and thereby proving the equivalence of (1) with (7) (proof lines 25887-25901).
Use the construction of derived limits to see that T(K, f) represents R Hom_A(A_f, K) in D(A), giving the equivalence of (1) with (3) (proof lines 25902-25906).

Write down the Ext spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Ext^p_A(A_f, H^q(K)) => Ext^{p+q}_A(A_f, K) and observe that it degenerates at E_2 because A_f has a length 1 projective resolution, so that the E_2 page has only two nonzero columns (proof lines 25909-25925).
Read off the short exact sequences 0 -> Ext^1_A(A_f, H^{p-1}(K)) -> Ext^p_A(A_f, K) -> Hom_A(A_f, H^p(K)) -> 0 and conclude that (4) and (5) are equivalent to (1) (proof lines 25926-25932).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, an element f, and a complex K in D(A), and establishes the equivalence of six genuine conditions (the seventh entry of the displayed list is the author's placeholder and contributes no mathematics): vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) for all n, vanishing of Hom in the derived category out of every object of D(A_f), the vanishing of T(K, f), the same condition degreewise on the cohomology, the pair of vanishings of Hom_A(A_f, H^p(K)) and Ext^1_A(A_f, H^p(K)), the vanishing of R Hom_A(A_f, K), and the invertibility of the explicitly displayed pro-product endomorphism (source lines 25849-25866). The proof runs three independent computations: it descends from Ext vanishing to Hom vanishing using a K-injective representative and the adjunction Hom_A(M, I) = Hom_{A_f}(M, Hom_A(A_f, I)) together with the fact that the resulting complex is K-injective and acyclic, hence homotopy equivalent to zero (proof lines 25869-25884); it writes down the explicit two-term free resolution of A_f with the displayed maps and identifies its Hom-dual with the pro-product endomorphism, which yields both the equivalence with condition (7) and the identification of T(K, f) with R Hom_A(A_f, K) (proof lines 25887-25906); and it uses the Ext spectral sequence of a two-term projective resolution, which degenerates at E_2 because the E_2 page then has only two nonzero columns, to obtain the short exact sequences comparing Ext^p_A(A_f, K) with Ext^1 and Hom of the cohomology (proof lines 25909-25932). The non-routine steps are the two-term resolution and the degeneration argument.
